speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand your episode of loss of consciousness; were you alone when it happened, and did anyone witness the event or see any shaking? Please describe the circumstances leading up to the fainting spell and how you felt immediately afterward.

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reflex Anoxic Seizure (post-micturition syncope). The timing of the loss of consciousness immediately following urination, combined with the rapid recovery and lack of incontinence, is highly specific to this condition caused by vagal stimulation. I am not requesting further tests as the clinical picture is definitive.
